common.placementGone: A server that is no longer connected

dns.noDomainsBody: Add the domain this server receives mail for.
dns.removeBody: The server stops receiving mail for it. Its DNS records are left as they are.
dns.noRecords: The mail server has not produced this domain's records yet.
dns.runCheck: Run "Check DNS" to see each record and whether it is published.

purposes.mx: Where mail for the domain is delivered
purposes.spf: Which servers may send as the domain
purposes.dkim: The key that signs outgoing mail
purposes.dmarc: What receivers do with mail that fails the checks
purposes.mtaSts: Tells senders to insist on TLS
purposes.tlsRpt: Where TLS failure reports are sent
purposes.service: Lets mail apps find the server
purposes.autoconfig: Lets mail apps set themselves up
purposes.caa: Which authority may issue the certificate

dns.addBody: The server generates its signing key; its records appear here to publish.
dns.catchAllBody: Mail to an address nobody has at this domain goes here instead of bouncing.
dns.catchAllHint: Catch-alls attract spam; leave empty to let unknown addresses bounce.
dns.publishBody: Nothing is changed until you apply. Records that are someone else's stay unless you replace them.
dns.replace: Replace the {count} {count, plural, one {record} other {records}} marked someone else's

schema.domain: That is not a domain name
schema.localPartChars: Use letters, digits, dots, dashes, underscores or plus
schema.address: That is not an email address
schema.passwordIdentity: That password is too close to the mailbox's own address. Pick something unrelated to it.
schema.passwordLineBreak: A password cannot contain a line break
schema.passwordBreached: That password has appeared in a known data breach. Pick a different one.

p25.label: SMTP
p25.purpose: Mail from other servers arrives here

p587.label: Submission
p587.purpose: Mail apps send through this with STARTTLS

p993.label: IMAP over TLS
p993.purpose: Mail apps read mail through this

p4190.label: ManageSieve
p4190.purpose: Mail apps edit filters through this

notes.hairpin: Polaris is on the same network as this server, and its router did not pass the connection back in. Mail from outside may still arrive.
notes.refused: The server answered that nothing is listening on this port.
notes.timeout25: Nothing answered in time. Many networks block outbound port 25, so this check cannot tell a closed port from one Polaris is not allowed to reach.
notes.timeout: Nothing answered in time. A firewall in front of the server may be dropping this port.

boxes.noneBody: Create one for each person or address that receives mail.
boxes.deleteBody: Every message in it is deleted with it, and mail to the address starts bouncing.
boxes.createIntro: Mail apps sign in with the address and this password over IMAP 993 and SMTP 465.
boxes.inMyMail: It is in your Mail as well.
boxes.name: Name
boxes.editIntro: Each part saves on its own.
boxes.newPasswordHint: Mail apps signed in with the old one are asked for this one.
boxes.warnNoMail: The mailbox was created. Your account cannot use Mail, so it was not added there.
boxes.warnNotAdded: The mailbox was created, but it could not be added to Mail.
boxes.warnNoConnectWhy: The mailbox was created. Mail could not connect to it yet ({reason}); add it from Mail once the server's DNS and certificate are in place.
boxes.warnNoConnect: The mailbox was created. Mail could not connect to it yet; add it from Mail once the server's DNS and certificate are in place.

errors.generic: That did not work. Try again in a moment.
errors.notInCatalog: Mail server is not in the catalog.
errors.installFailed: Mail server could not be installed. Try again in a moment.
errors.uninstallFailed: Mail server could not be uninstalled. Try again in a moment.
errors.setupRunning: Setup is still running. Wait for it to stop first.

refusals.notFound: That mail server was not found.
refusals.notYourOrg: You cannot manage this organization's mail servers.
refusals.noAdmin: This mail server has no administrator credential yet. Run setup again.
refusals.notInstalledHint: Mail server is not installed. Install it from the Marketplace first.
refusals.uninstallOwner: Only whoever installed Mail server, or an administrator, can uninstall it.
refusals.notRunning: This mail server is not running yet. Finish setting it up first.
refusals.reportTooBig: That report unpacks to more than any real report does.
refusals.reportDamaged: That compressed report is damaged, or unpacks to more than any real report does.
refusals.zipTooBig: That zip file unpacks to more than any real report does.
refusals.noReport: No DMARC report was found in that file.
refusals.settingUp: This mail server is still being set up.
refusals.connectCloudflare: Connect a Cloudflare API token under Integrations to publish records from here.
refusals.domainMissing: That domain is not on this mail server.
refusals.ruleMissing: That rule is not on this mail server.
refusals.firstDomain: The server's first domain holds Polaris's own accounts and cannot be removed.
refusals.mailboxMissing: That mailbox is not on this mail server.
refusals.polarisMailbox: Polaris sends its own mail from this mailbox, so it is left as it is.
refusals.aliasDomain: An alias names a domain that is not on this mail server.
refusals.forwardLoop: A forward cannot send mail back to its own address.
refusals.forwardMissing: That forward is not on this mail server.
refusals.relaySecret: Enter the relay's password or API key.
refusals.serverNotYours: That server was not found among yours.
refusals.swarm: That server deploys through a swarm, which hides the address every incoming connection comes from. A mail server needs it for spam filtering and sender checks, so choose a server that runs plain containers.
refusals.adminMissing: The administrator credential is missing. Remove this server and set it up again.
refusals.serviceMissing: The mail server's service is missing. Repair from the start.
refusals.placementGone: The server this was to run on is no longer connected.
refusals.swarmShort: That server deploys through a swarm, which a mail server cannot run behind.
refusals.noEnvironment: The mail server's project has no environment.
refusals.adminRejected: After the restart the mail server did not accept Polaris's administrator account, so the setup credential was put back. Run setup again.
refusals.signingKey: The event signing key is missing. Remove this server and set it up again.
refusals.notJmapSession: The mail server answered with something that is not a JMAP session.
refusals.noMailboxMail: The mail server's session does not offer this mailbox's mail.
refusals.attachment: The mail server would not hand that attachment over.
refusals.failedRequest: The mail server failed to answer that request.
refusals.notJmap: The mail server answered with something that is not JMAP.
refusals.noAnswer: The mail server did not answer that request
refusals.serviceGone: The mail server's service no longer exists.
refusals.noAddress: Polaris does not know this machine's address yet.
refusals.downHere: The mail server is not answering on this machine.
refusals.hostUnreachable: Polaris could not reach the server the mail server runs on.
refusals.downThere: The mail server is not answering on its server.
refusals.domainGone: {domain} is missing from the mail server. Repair it from the start.
refusals.domainGoneShort: {domain} is missing from the mail server. Repair from the start.
refusals.needsVerified: Publishing from here needs {domain} verified under Domains. Until then, add the records listed under it at your DNS host.
refusals.ownDnsAccount: {domain} is on this Polaris's own DNS account. Verify it under Domains, then add it here.
refusals.notAZone: {domain} is not a zone in the Cloudflare account Polaris is connected to.
refusals.tooManyRules: A mail server holds at most {max} rules.
refusals.domainHasMailboxes: {domain} still has {count, plural, one {# mailbox} other {# mailboxes}}. Remove them first.
refusals.reservedAddress: {address} is Polaris's own. Choose another name.
refusals.hostnameTaken: {hostname} already has a mail server here.
refusals.didNotStart: The mail server did not start: {reason}

steps.sender: Setting Polaris up to send through it
steps.reports: Setting up the DMARC report mailbox

overview.repairFrom: Repair by running setup again from
overview.removeHint: Removing it here stops Polaris managing it. The service, its volumes and the mail in them stay in Deploy until you delete them there.
overview.removeBody: Its service and mail stay in Deploy. Rules on incoming mail and filed DMARC reports are deleted.

health.title: Health
health.knocked: Ports knocked on at <mono>{address}</mono>, from where Polaris runs.
health.knockedAt: Ports knocked on at <mono>{address}</mono>, from where Polaris runs, {when}.

notes.serviceMissing: The mail server's service is missing. Repair it from the start.
notes.unreachable: The mail server could not be reached.
notes.notAnswering: The mail server is not answering. It may be stopped or restarting.
notes.adminRejected: The mail server no longer accepts Polaris's administrator account. Repair it from the administrator step.
notes.noAddress: There is no address to check it at yet.
notes.certSoon: The certificate expires within two weeks and has not been renewed yet.
notes.certNoAnswer: Port 465 did not answer, so the certificate could not be read.
notes.certNoTls: Port 465 did not complete a secure connection.
notes.resolversSilent: The public resolvers did not answer for this name.
notes.cannotLookUp: Polaris cannot look this record type up.
notes.dnssecOnly: Only meaningful on a zone signed with DNSSEC; publish it yourself if yours is.
notes.spfCovers: The SPF already published covers this server.
notes.spfAdds: Adds this server to the SPF already published, keeping everything in it.
notes.dmarcKept: A DMARC policy is already published; it is kept.
notes.mxElsewhere: Mail for this domain goes somewhere else today. It is left there unless you replace it.
notes.somethingElseKept: Something else is published at this name. It is left there unless you replace it.
notes.spfTwo: There are two SPF records, which makes both invalid. Keep one.
notes.spfMore: An SPF record is published with more in it than this server needs. Mail still passes.
notes.spfMissing: The published SPF record does not include this server.
notes.dmarcOther: A different DMARC policy is published. It is valid; reports may go elsewhere.
notes.nothingYet: Nothing is published at this name yet.
notes.optional: Not published. Mail works without it.
notes.somethingElse: Something else is published at this name.
notes.ptrNoAddress: There is no public address for this server yet, so its reverse name cannot be checked.
notes.ptrLookupFailed: The reverse name could not be looked up just now. Check again in a moment.
notes.hostUnresolved: {host} does not resolve yet, and this network has no public address to check instead. Publish its DNS records first.
notes.certRefused: Mail apps will refuse this certificate ({reason}). It is usually the engine's own until its certificate for {host} is issued.
notes.outside: Outside {root}; add it at your DNS host.
notes.ptrSetBy: A reverse name is set by whoever gives you the address - the hosting provider or the internet provider - not at your DNS host. Ask them to point {address} at {host}.
notes.ptrNone: {address} has no reverse name. Several large receivers refuse mail from an address with none, before they read anything else about it.
notes.ptrNotConfirmed: {address} reverse-resolves to {pointer}, and {pointer} does not resolve back to it. A receiver checking both reads that as no reverse name at all.
notes.ptrOtherName: {address} reverse-resolves to {pointer}, not to {host}. Mail is accepted more readily when the greeting name and the reverse name are the same.
notes.ptrGeneric: {pointer} reads as an address a provider hands out in a block. Receivers that judge on the shape of the name file mail from one as junk even when everything else passes.
notes.ptrPass: {address} reverse-resolves to {pointer}, and it resolves back. This is the name the server greets with.
notes.hostLookupFailed: {host} could not be looked up just now. Check again in a moment.
notes.publishAPointing: Publish an A record for {host} pointing at {address} at your DNS host.
notes.publishA: Publish an A record for {host} at your DNS host.
notes.greetingUnresolved: {host} does not resolve. It is the name this server greets other servers with, the name on its certificate and the target of its MX record, so nothing reaches it and its mail is refused by servers that check the greeting.
notes.greetingNoAddress: {host} resolves, but there is no known public address to compare it with.
notes.greetingMismatch: {host} resolves to {addresses}, and mail leaves from {address}. A receiver checking the greeting against the sending address will not see a match.
notes.greetingPass: {host} resolves to {address}, which is where mail leaves from.
notes.adminMailbox: Polaris manages this mail server with this account.
notes.senderMailbox: Polaris sends its own mail from this mailbox.
notes.reportsMailbox: DMARC reports about this server's domains arrive here; Polaris reads and files them.

list.noneBody: Polaris installs one on this machine or a server you enrolled, then walks its DNS through with you.

uninstall.title: Uninstall Mail server
uninstall.removeFirst: Remove your mail servers first. Each one's page has Remove from Polaris at the bottom of its overview.
uninstall.body: It leaves the menu and search. Nothing runs for it, so nothing is stopped, and you can install it again from the Marketplace.

setup.intro: It runs as a service in Deploy, with ports 25, 465, 587, 993 and 4190 published on the machine you choose.
setup.runsOnHint: A server that deploys through a swarm cannot run one.
setup.firstDomainHint: The domain mail is received for, like example.com.
setup.hostnameHint: What its certificate is for and what MX points at. It must resolve to the machine it runs on.

install.title: Install Mail server from the Marketplace
install.body: Mail at your own domains: SPF, DKIM and DMARC written and checked, mailboxes and aliases. Installing downloads nothing - a server is set up only when you choose a machine for it.
install.bodyAsk: Mail at your own domains: SPF, DKIM and DMARC written and checked, mailboxes and aliases. Ask somebody who can install apps to add it.

page.title: Mail server
page.description: Send and receive mail at your own domains, with the DNS it needs published and checked from here.

rules.noneBody: Get a notification when mail you care about arrives: an invoice address, a monitoring sender.
rules.summary: To {to}, from {from}{spam, select, yes {, spam included} other {}}
rules.intro: Use * for any run of characters, like *@bank.example. Empty matches everything.
rules.includeSpam: Also for mail the spam filter caught

reports.collected: {messages, plural, one {# message} other {# messages}} read, {filed, plural, one {# new report} other {# new reports}}.
reports.uploadFailed: The report could not be uploaded.
reports.filed: Filed {count, plural, one {# report} other {# reports}}.
reports.otherDomain: That report is about a domain this server does not hold.
reports.address: Receivers send reports to <mono>{address}</mono> and its alias at each domain.
reports.noneBody: Receivers send them daily once your DMARC record is published and mail from your domains reaches them.
reports.failHint: An address that always fails is either somebody sending as your domain, or a real sender of yours that is not in SPF or not signing with DKIM.
reports.inRange: {count, plural, one {# report} other {# reports}} in this range

forwards.noneBody: Send an address's mail on to other people without giving it a mailbox.
forwards.deleteBody: Mail to the address starts bouncing. Nothing already delivered is touched.
forwards.intro: Receivers may treat forwarded mail as suspicious when the sender's domain enforces DMARC.
forwards.sendToHint: One address per line, or separated by commas.

sending.nowDirect: Mail now goes straight to each recipient.
sending.nowRelay: Mail now goes out through the relay.
sending.spfHint: Adds {include} to each domain's SPF in the DNS plan.
sending.secretHint: Leave empty to keep the one saved.
sending.channel: Polaris sends its own mail through this server as an email channel, under <link>Management, Email</link>.

backups.intro: Each copy is the engine's own export, taken with the server paused for as long as it runs, so every mailbox is caught at the same moment. Mail sent meanwhile is retried by the sender. Restoring pauses it again and puts the whole server back.
backups.notRunningBody: It can be protected once setup has finished.
backups.volumes: Its volumes are also still copied as files, from before:

notices.notAnswering: The mail server is not answering.
notices.spam: The spam filter marked it as spam.
notices.ceiling: This rule has matched often in the last ten minutes; further matches are not notified until the window ends.
